description: Renovate runs as the GitHub App on this account, not as a self-hosted workflow. That is what makes its commits signed: an App installation token creates them through the API and GitHub signs them with its web-flow key, which verify-pr-signatures requires. A PAT gets attribution but no signature, which is why the self-hosted setup needed every PR re-signed by hand.

platformCommit is gone with it. It moved the committer off renovate@whitesourcesoftware.com and onto this account, which fixed attribution and left the signature failing -- the App fixes both, and the option does nothing for an App.

The shared jdwlabs preset supplies the schedule, limits, labels and vulnerability handling, so those are not restated here. Only the rules that are specific to this repository stay below: merging this repo is deploying.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions only, and deliberately not the container images. Merging this repository is deploying -- the Application auto-syncs with selfHeal -- so an automerge here has to be something that cannot change a rendered manifest. A workflow file is exactly that: helm renders the same output before and after, so the sync is a no-op and nothing in the cluster moves. Every image tag fails that test, including the agent and console-bridge ones that are not otherwise excluded: they recreate a pod, and an unattended pod recreation is what cost ~29 MB of world data on 2026-08-30.

The server agent. It lives in its own Deployment, not the game StatefulSet, so a bump recreates the agent pod and never touches the server players are connected to. That Deployment is RollingUpdate with maxSurge 1 / maxUnavailable 0, and /readyz reports a standby as ready while a still-authenticating pod reports 503 -- so the replacement is in the game before the incumbent leaves, and a release costs a handover rather than an absence. That handover is what makes this safe to merge unattended. Own group and not held to the weekly window: the server updates itself, so a stale agent is offline, and a shared group would make this wait on every other pending update. mc-console-bridge is deliberately not here: it is a sidecar of the game server pod.

PR-only, not auto-merged. The original reasoning was that clients need a current server, with RollingUpdate and the nightly backup as the safety net -- but image.tag only versions itzg's tooling, not the server binary, so this never delivered a game version at all. What kept the server current was the pod restart it happened to cause, and versionCheck now does that deliberately every hour with player notice. Meanwhile RollingUpdate is the mechanism that recreates the pod, and an unattended recreation is what migrated the world PVC and cost ~29 MB on 2026-08-30 -- so the cited safety net was the hazard, and a backup is a recovery path rather than a guard. Merging these by hand costs nothing in client connectivity and keeps pod recreations attended. See docs/incidents/2026-08-30-fwb-world-data-loss.md.
kubectl/bash toolbox and the backup exporter's busybox -- version drift here has no client-compatibility pressure, so these stay PR-only for a human to merge.

The world map. Its Deployment owns its own volume and is not in the game StatefulSet, so a bump recreates the map pod only: the page is away for a restart and nothing players are connected to moves. That is what makes it safe to merge unattended.

The crew lab's worker. It runs only against the lab server in its own app, never FWB, so a bump recreates the crew pods and nothing players are connected to moves. That is what makes it safe to merge unattended.

The AFK bots. They are Deployments, not the game StatefulSet, so a bump recreates a bot pod and never touches the server or its volume; a bot reconnects on its own. This used to be off because the image bakes in one Bedrock version's protocol data and was meant to move with a hand-reviewed server bump. The server now updates itself hourly, so a bot that waits for a human is offline after every Mojang release (2026-10-27: both bots down ~8.5 h). Own group and not held to the weekly window for the same reason as the agent.

The wildlife add-on packs' image runs as an init container on the game server pod, so a bump restarts the world. The tag moves by hand, when a pack changes, together with tools/crew-lab-kit-rev.py --write, which puts the new tag into UNIT_KIT_REV so the unit-kit gate holds the restart until nobody is online. It matches a different package from the map-pack rule below, so their order does not matter.

The game server's init step, which installs the map's script pack, carries the map's image. Every update to that file is off: the map rule above merges unattended because a map bump restarts only the map pod, and an init container on the game server pod is the one place that is not true. On 2026-10-06 the same update moved this tag and restarted the world with nobody watching. The tag there moves by hand, when the pack changes. This rule is last so that it wins.
